points.t: Scalp itch (or none), nape and behind-ear excoriation, a **live louse** on detection combing.
*Pediculus humanus capitis* crawls head-to-head; itch is hypersensitivity to saliva.
Only live infestation: **wet combing** or **dimeticone 4%** (repeat after 7 days); check the household.
No live louse, no treatment. Pubic lice on a child’s eyelashes → **safeguarding**.

cause.lead: A crawling insect that glues its eggs near the scalp.
points: Spread by **direct head-to-head contact**: lice crawl; they can’t jump, fly or swim.
Off the scalp they die in about **1–2 days**: hats and brushes rarely matter.
Eggs glued near the scalp hatch in 7–10 days; adults live 3–4 weeks.
**Nits** = empty egg cases moving out with hair growth: far from the scalp = old.
Itch can take **4–6 weeks**; many children never itch. **Not** poor hygiene.

visuals.caption: A six-legged head louse gripping a hair, live eggs cemented to the shafts within a few millimetres of the scalp, and an empty white nit case further out. A fine-toothed detection comb finds live lice.
visuals.alt: Magnified hair shafts with a head louse, nits and a detection comb

points: Itch (often absent), tickling, excoriation **behind the ears and at the nape**.
Live grey-brown lice that move away from light.
Eggs and nits **cemented** to the shaft: they don’t slide off.
Complications: impetigo, occipital nodes, eczematisation, poor sleep, stigma.

items.name: Adult louse
items.t: Six legs with claws for gripping hair.

items.name: Eggs / nits
items.t: Cemented to the shaft near the scalp.

points: Fine-toothed plastic comb on wet conditioned (or dry) hair: more sensitive than looking.
Check **everyone**; treat only those with live lice, **same day**.
Dandruff and hair casts brush or slide off; nits stay put.

cards.name: Dandruff / seborrhoeic
cards.clue: Flaky scale that brushes off; no lice.

cards.name: Hair casts
cards.clue: Tubular casts that slide along the shaft.

cards.name: Scalp psoriasis
cards.clue: Thick scale beyond the hairline; nails, body plaques.

cards.name: Tinea capitis
cards.clue: Broken hairs, alopecia, black dots; mycology.

cards.name: Nape impetigo
cards.clue: Honey crust: look for lice as the driver.

manage.lead: Treat only when a live louse is found (NICE CKS).

points: **Wet combing** (Bug Busting): conditioner + detection comb on days **1, 5, 9 and 13**; check day 17.
Fine for infants, pregnancy, asthma and eczema.

rx.dose: Dry hair, leave overnight (check product), wash out
rx.note: CKS first line in pregnancy, breastfeeding, young children, asthma / eczema. Flammable while on hair.
Only chemical still recommended; resistance common; aqueous if asthma / eczema.

points: Detection-comb 2–3 days after finishing, and again after 7 days.
Live lice persist: check technique, then **switch mode of action**.
Oral ivermectin or co-trimoxazole are specialist / off-label: **refer**.

limits.t: Permethrin creme rinse, shampoos alone, herbal oils, electric combs, ‘preventive’ treatment.
No school exclusion, boil-washing or fumigation.

items.t: Pubic lice on a child’s **eyelashes** → safeguarding pathway.
Infant **under 6 months**: wet combing only; seek advice if it fails.
Extensive secondary infection, severe eczematous scalp, or suspected misdiagnosis.

pearls.t: Asthma / eczema: wet combing or aqueous dimeticone; avoid alcohol lotions.
Itch can last a few days after cure; leftover nits ≠ failure.
Course materials recommending permethrin are out of step with CKS.

quiz.a: A live louse (found by detection combing). Nits alone don’t.
Days 1, 5, 9 and 13, with a check on day 17.
On dry hair, left on (often overnight per product), washed out, repeated after 7 days.

quiz.q: Is permethrin recommended for head lice in the UK?
quiz.a: No: unsuitable contact time and widespread resistance.

quiz.q: Does a child need to stay off school?
